name: Pulsar Ridgeline
summary: Unknown Pleasures-style stacked ridgelines where the checkout peaks go flat the minute the deploy lands.
look: Near-black field with occluding off-white ridgelines stacked like a pulsar plot; teal takes over for Pulse and one coral ridge marks 09:42. Mono minute labels, Instrument Serif headlines.

components.name: Ridge line
components.role: occluding filled stroke, one per minute, front lines hide back ones

components.name: Signal ridge
components.role: the front line redrawn as the Acme pulse shape

components.name: Time gutter
components.role: mono minute labels every 5 ridges on the left

components.name: Event ridge
components.role: one coral line + dashed guide at the anomaly minute

components.name: Stat column
components.role: serif −18% with mono context on the right

components.name: Black field
components.role: deep near-black ground, off-white strokes, no grid

motion.name: Ridge print
motion.how: each new ridge slides up 17 px with power1.out 0.25 s — one 8th note at 120 BPM — the stack scrolls like a pen plotter

motion.name: Morph to pulse
motion.how: front ridge path morphs into the mark's pulse shape, expo.inOut 0.75 s, landing on the drop; stroke goes white → teal

motion.name: Flatten
motion.how: post-09:42 ridges scale Y to 0.42 with sine.inOut 0.5 s, staggered 0.05 s, so the flattening ripples down on the snare

story: Hook: 38 dashboards as a wall of noisy ridges. Drop: the noise calms and the front ridge becomes the Acme pulse line. Proof: one ridge per minute of checkouts, a coral ridge at 09:42 and flatter peaks after deploy #2231, −18%, Roll back. CTA: a calm teal ridge field, You ship. Pulse watches., Start free.
adapt: Any time-series with a rhythm (requests per minute, builds per hour, messages per second) can be stacked as ridges; swap the pulse shape for your own logo line and show your anomaly as the moment the peaks change.

references.note: Peter Saville's cover: CP 1919 pulsar ridgeline, reversed to white on black

fit.risk: Iconic but moody; the pop-culture reference can overpower the product if the ridges are not clearly labelled as data.
